_meta.description: Typical OCI service provisioning times for JEP phase timeline planning
_meta.purpose: Makes JEP phase timelines defensible with empirical baselines. Values are 'typical observed' ranges, not SLAs.
_meta.methodology: Derived from Oracle documentation, official blog posts, community experience, and operator observations. Where Oracle docs state a range, that range is preserved. Times assume normal tenancy quota and no capacity constraints.
_meta.disclaimer: These are planning estimates, not contractual SLAs. Actual times vary with region load, shape availability, and tenancy limits. FastConnect and ADB-D times depend on physical/third-party factors.

vcn_and_subnets.notes: VCN + subnets + route tables + security lists are near-instant API operations. Terraform apply for a full VCN with 3 subnets, IGW, NAT GW, and route tables typically completes in under 30 seconds.

drg_and_attachment.notes: DRG creation is fast; VCN attachment and route propagation add a minute or two.

load_balancer_flexible.notes: Flexible Load Balancer (Layer 7) or Network Load Balancer reach ACTIVE state quickly. Backend health checks add a minute after instance registration.

fastconnect_virtual_circuit_partner.range: Minutes to hours for OCI-side provisioning; days to weeks for physical circuit activation

breakdown.physical_cross_connect_colo: 1–4 weeks depending on facility and provider
breakdown.bgp_session_establishment: Minutes once physical layer is up

fastconnect_virtual_circuit_partner.notes: FastConnect OCI-side objects provision in minutes. The real lead time is the physical last-mile and partner activation. Plan 2–4 weeks end-to-end in JEPs for new circuits; existing partner connections can be 1–3 business days.
fastconnect_virtual_circuit_partner.plan_as_jep: 2–4 weeks (new circuit) | 1–3 business days (existing partner port)

waf_policy.notes: OCI WAF policy (Web Application Firewall) is documented to become active within 15 minutes of creation. DNS propagation to WAF edge may add additional time.

compute_instance_flex_vm.notes: VM.Standard.E5.Flex and similar VM shapes launch within minutes per Oracle Compute FAQ. Larger shapes (64 OCPU) and custom images may be at the higher end.

compute_instance_bare_metal_gpu.notes: BM.GPU4.8 and BM.GPU.H100.8 take longer than VMs due to physical host allocation and driver initialization.

bastion_service_session.notes: OCI Bastion service itself provisions in under a minute. Individual managed SSH sessions or port-forwarding sessions activate within seconds of creation.

oke_cluster_control_plane.notes: OKE control plane (API server, etcd) provisions separately from worker nodes. Enhanced clusters with VCN-native pod networking take slightly longer.

oke_node_pool_worker_nodes.notes: Worker nodes are compute instances plus Kubernetes bootstrap. Oracle states up to 30 minutes for full cluster (control plane + workers).

oke_cluster_total.notes: Oracle documentation states 'up to 30 minutes to provision all resources for your cluster'.

autonomous_database_serverless.notes: ADB Serverless (ATP or ADW) typically provisions in a few minutes. Oracle documentation states it may take longer for smaller shapes, but generally < 15 minutes. Always Free tier may queue longer.

autonomous_database_dedicated_full_stack.notes: ADB-D (Autonomous Database Dedicated on Exadata Cloud Service) requires provisioning the full Exadata Infrastructure → VM Cluster → Container DB → ADB stack in sequence. The VM Cluster step dominates timing. Plan for a full working day.
autonomous_database_dedicated_full_stack.plan_as_jep: 5–6 hours (or 1 business day to allow for any issues)

mysql_heatwave.notes: MySQL HeatWare DB system provisions in under 20 minutes for standard shapes.

base_db_vm_dbsystem.notes: OCI Base DB (DB System on VM) takes longer than ADB Serverless due to OS + Oracle DB software provisioning.

object_storage_bucket.notes: Object Storage bucket creation is near-instant API operation. IAM policy propagation for access may take 30–60 seconds.

block_volume.notes: Block Volume creation is fast. Attachment to a compute instance adds another 15–30 seconds. iSCSI login and OS-side formatting are additional steps post-provisioning.

file_storage_mount_target.notes: OCI File Storage Service (NFS) mount target creation takes a few minutes.

oci_vault.notes: OCI Vault (software-protected) provisions in under a minute. HSM-backed (Virtual Private Vault) may take slightly longer due to dedicated HSM partition allocation.

kms_key.notes: Key creation within an existing vault is near-instant. First key in a new vault requires vault to be ACTIVE first.

oci_certificates_ssl.notes: OCI Certificates service (internal CA or imported cert) provisions quickly. Third-party CA issuance timelines are outside OCI control.

jep_phase_planning_summary.description: Rolled-up time blocks for JEP phase planning. These are wall-clock estimates assuming sequential provisioning by a single operator with pre-staged Terraform.

day_1_infrastructure_foundation.notes: Entire networking foundation via Terraform in ~15 minutes

compute_and_oke.notes: OKE dominates at up to 30 minutes. Compute VMs add ~5 minutes in parallel or sequence.

database_adb_serverless.notes: Can run in parallel with OKE provisioning

database_adb_dedicated.notes: Must be planned as a dedicated half-day activity; book a maintenance window

security_stack.notes: WAF policy activation (15 min) is the long pole; Vault + KMS is < 2 minutes

connectivity_fastconnect.notes: Physical circuit lead time dominates. Must be ordered in Phase 0 / pre-engagement. OCI-side configuration is done in minutes but cannot be tested until carrier activates the circuit.

total_cloud_provisioning_excluding_fastc.notes: A full OCI foundation stack (VCN, OKE, ADB Serverless, Load Balancer, Vault, WAF) can be provisioned by Terraform in 1–2 hours. ADB-D adds ~6 hours if required.
